note: One position of the minor pentatonic scale, four jobs, each the same dots turned a new way: one note per beat over the metronome, only the roots with the whole neck above, every dot over a faster backing track, then a drill of the learner's own made by changing one thing (folded in from guitar-beginner-position-1-at-80-then-your-own-drill, whose faster tempo is now the moves' range). One position is on the screen, so no position number anywhere; key and tempo are moves (any key, 60 to 90), named only as params.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic: the dots, the roots, your own drill
exercise.why: A phrase sounds finished when it ends on the root, so learn the shape and where its roots sit together: then anything you make up has somewhere to land.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Under it is the neck with the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale: each dot is a note to play, and the ringed dots are the {{1}} notes.
Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string and play both dots on each string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way, one note per beat.
Practice until your fingers find the next dot without you looking.

Now only the {{1}} notes are in play, and above the dots the whole neck shows where they sit. Hop between the ones inside the frame in any order.
Practice until you can go to each {{1}} without hunting for it.
{{?key}}In another key the dots sit on other frets, and the roots keep their places among them.
Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass, faster than the metronome was. Play all the dots again, low to high and back, starting from a different {{1}} each time.

Keep the backing track going and make a drill of your own by changing one thing: the direction, the rhythm, or which dots you play. Play it until it feels easy, then change another thing.
End each run on a ringed {{1}} and listen for how it sounds finished.
